top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a mature, experimentally robust discovery: the magic-wavelength lattice removes Doppler, recoil and first-order light shifts, and independent laboratories have reproduced fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. This opened a genuinely new regime of precision in time and frequency measurement, and the award goes to the scientific achievement rather than a promised application. The two-laureate allocation matches the invention (Katori's magic-wavelength proposal) and its realisation and development to the 1e-18 level (Ye), and the citation scope is well bounded. A prize is clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; optical lattice clocks lie outside my superconducting-circuit work, though as WACQT director I have general ties to precision quantum technology.
